title: Gloving Tutorial: Whips, Tunnels, and Circle Move [Frosty] {HC} {LJ}

observation_window.sampling: provider default; not continuous motion capture

extraction.teacher_style: The instructor speaks conversationally while demonstrating hand and arm techniques close to the webcam camera. He focuses on key mechanical points, such as bending wrists and incorporating shoulder rotation, to enhance visual illusions.

lesson_structure.note: Instructor introduces himself and states the video topic of whips, tunnels, and circle moves.
Instructor lists foundational prerequisite moves like basic finger rolls and overhand waves.
Instructor demonstrates and breaks down forward and backward whips using slow motion movement close to the camera.
Instructor explains how bending wrists 90 degrees and incorporating shoulder rotation enhances the whip move.
Instructor demonstrates and breaks down tunnels using two-handed whip techniques.
Instructor shows how incorrect palm angles affect light shows for the audience.

cues: bend your wrist as far back as possible
common_mistakes: Not bending wrists back 90 degrees, resulting in smaller circles and sloppy illusions.
Having palms facing outward to the sides instead of directly toward the viewer receiving the light show.

steps_taught.name: Whips
steps_taught.description: Starting from an L-shaped tut position, roll the hand outward into an open hand and back in to create circular light motion.

steps_taught.name: Backward Whips
steps_taught.description: Starting facing inward, unroll the hand outward and spin to return back into tut position.

steps_taught.name: Tunnels
steps_taught.description: A two-handed whip concept executing stacked alternating finger rolls moving outward and inward.

what_works: Close-up webcam perspective clearly isolates small hand and finger movements.
Explanations break down specific mechanical adjustments like wrist angles and shoulder pivot.
what_hinders: Lack of rhythmic counting or structured beats for execution.
Fast motion occasionally causes camera motion blur as noted by the instructor.

quotes.text: I'm going to do it slow motion because it's a webcam.
You start off with an L-shaped sort of tut.
You want to bend your wrist as far back as possible.
I call tunnels pretty much two-handed whips.
Your palms is facing the person giving a light show to.

evidence_segments.cannot_infer: exact movement timing without count breakdown

evidence_segments.observation: Instructor shows reverse whip motion, performing continuous circular unrolling and closing sequence with hands.
evidence_segments.cannot_infer: full speed trajectory due to webcam frame rate blur

evidence_segments.observation: Instructor contrasts halfway-bent wrist positions with 90-degree bent wrist positions to show circle scale differences.
evidence_segments.cannot_infer: exact joint extension angle without side view

extraction.distinctive_method: Emphasizes anatomical mechanics, specifically shoulder torque and 90-degree wrist flexibility, to optimize visual trail scope during hand performances.
